facts.text: The simplest camera simulation uses an ideal pinhole camera with distortion and noise.
facts.quote: At the simplest level, camera simulation uses an ideal pinhole camera with distortion and noise.

facts.text: Higher-fidelity camera simulation renders physically based materials and lights and adds calibrated lens distortion, point-spread or MTF effects, vignetting, chromatic and spectral response, rolling or global shutter, exposure, gain, shot and read noise, saturation, and the image-signal-processing chain.
facts.quote: Higher-fidelity models render physically based materials and lights, then add calibrated lens distortion, point-spread or MTF effects, vignetting, chromatic and spectral response, rolling or global shutter, exposure, gain, shot and read noise, saturation and the image-signal-processing chain.

facts.text: Path tracing handles indirect light and specular reflection more faithfully than simple raster rendering.
facts.quote: Path tracing handles indirect light and specular reflection more faithfully than simple raster rendering.

facts.text: Camera simulation rendering uses game engines or path tracing, with open-source CARLA and commercial tools from several vendors as examples.
facts.quote: Rendering is based on game engines or path tracing (open-source CARLA; commercial tools from several vendors).

facts.text: ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D version 1.0 (2025) standardizes refractive index, surface roughness, permeability, and measured wavelength- and angle-dependent reflection so a single asset can carry sensor-relevant properties.
facts.quote: ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D (version 1.0, 2025) standardizes properties such as refractive index, surface roughness, permeability and measured wavelength- and angle-dependent reflection so one asset can carry sensor-relevant properties

facts.text: A visually convincing simulated RGB image can still be physically wrong at the detector.
facts.quote: The main camera trap is that a visually convincing RGB image can still be physically wrong at the detector.

facts.text: Camera glare and low-sun effects depend on the lens and cover window, internal ghost paths, coatings, aperture, sensor saturation, and ISP.
facts.quote: Glare and low sun depend on the lens and cover window, internal ghost paths, coatings, aperture, sensor saturation and ISP

facts.text: Camera behavior in darkness depends on gain, noise, and HDR.
facts.quote: darkness depends on gain, noise and HDR

facts.text: LED work lights can introduce spectra and temporal flicker that an ordinary RGB renderer does not represent.
facts.quote: LED work lights can introduce spectra and temporal flicker that an ordinary RGB renderer does not represent.

facts.text: Public evidence jointly validating glare and low sun, darkness, and LED work-light spectral and flicker effects for construction or mining cameras was not found.
facts.quote: Public evidence validating all those effects jointly for construction or mining cameras was not found.

facts.text: SynFog (2024) built a fog chamber and a one-to-one virtual twin in Blender; simulated per-channel trends consistently followed real captures as fog density increased. This is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: SynFog (2024) built a fog chamber and a one-to-one virtual twin of it in Blender and showed that simulated per-channel trends "consistently follow" real captures as fog density increases

facts.text: Physics-based rain rendering on real images in Tremblay et al. (2020) degrades detection, segmentation, and depth estimation as a function of rainfall rate. This is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Physics-based rain rendering on real images (Tremblay et al., 2020) degrades detection, segmentation and depth estimation as a function of rainfall rate

facts.text: Learned camera simulation methods include GANs, diffusion models, and neural rendering.
facts.quote: Learned methods include GANs, diffusion models and neural rendering

facts.text: NeuroNCAP (2024) reports a minimal real-to-sim gap for neural rendering of nuScenes logs in open loop. This is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: NeuroNCAP (2024) reports a "minimal" real-to-sim gap for neural rendering of nuScenes logs in open loop

facts.text: In NeuroNCAP (2024), across 14 sequences, UniAD scored 0.490 NDS on real images and 0.489 NDS on rendered images. This is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: across 14 sequences, UniAD scored 0.490 NDS on real and 0.489 on rendered images

facts.text: In NeuroNCAP (2024), across 14 sequences, VAD's NDS score dropped from 0.449 on real images to 0.413 on rendered images. This is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: across 14 sequences, UniAD scored 0.490 NDS on real and 0.489 on rendered images, while VAD dropped from 0.449 to 0.413

facts.text: Several vendors offer image injection into a camera's processing unit for hardware-in-the-loop testing, including Ansys AVxcelerate's "HiL-ready image injection."
facts.quote: For hardware-in-the-loop, image injection into the camera's processing unit is offered by several vendors (for example Ansys AVxcelerate "HiL-ready image injection")

facts.text: Over-the-air screen or projector stimulation is used for camera hardware-in-the-loop testing.
facts.quote: over-the-air screen or projector stimulation is also used [59]

facts.text: Screen or projector stimulation keeps camera optics and imager electronics in the test loop.
facts.quote: A screen or projector keeps optics and imager electronics in the loop

facts.text: Digital video injection bypasses real camera optics, so lens flare, soiling on the real lens, and the full high-dynamic-range response are not physically tested.
facts.quote: digital video injection bypasses the real optics, so lens flare, soiling on the real lens and the full high-dynamic-range response are not tested physically.
